title: 2023 HMMT November Guts Problem 5
statement:
Let \(A B C D E\) be a convex pentagon such that

\[\begin{aligned}
& A B+B C+C D+D E+E A=64 \text { and } \\
& A C+C E+E B+B D+D A=72 .
\end{aligned}\]

Compute the perimeter of the convex pentagon whose vertices are the midpoints of the sides of \(A B C D E\).

solutions.text:
By the midsegment theorem on triangles \(A B C, B C D, \ldots, D E A\), the side lengths of the said pentagons are \(A C / 2, B D / 2, C E / 2, D A / 2\), and \(E B / 2\). Thus, the answer is

\[\frac{A C+B D+C E+D A+E B}{2}=\frac{72}{2}=36\]
